verdict.summary: You create a public connection in the Notion Developer portal and it works over OAuth right away. Per Notion's docs, a Marketplace listing is optional and is the only step Notion reviews. The one decision you can't undo is the installation scope: choose 'Any workspace' if you want people outside your own workspaces to install it.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min (plus a few hours if you write and submit a Marketplace listing)
verdict.approval_wait: None for OAuth use. 5-10 business days if you choose to submit a Marketplace listing.

gates.name: Public connection (just created, your own workspace)
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own Notion account through your own client ID and secret, and share pages with the connection using the page picker.
limits: Each user who authorizes can only share the pages they choose in the page picker
Access is set by the capabilities you pick, not by OAuth scope strings

gates.name: Public connection, unlisted (invited users)
gates.unlocks: Other people can install the connection through your OAuth link. With 'Selected workspaces only', this is limited to the workspaces you choose.
limits: 'Selected workspaces only' connections can never be listed on the Marketplace, and installation scope can't be changed after creation
Every workspace member has to authorize separately; one user's authorization doesn't cover anyone else
No install caps or rate limits for unreviewed connections were found

gates.name: Any-workspace public connection (optional Marketplace listing)
gates.unlocks: Any Notion user can authorize via OAuth. A Marketplace listing adds discoverability in Notion's directory.
limits: Only the Marketplace listing is reviewed. Notion says a listing isn't required for OAuth use
Only Any-workspace connections can be listed
Listing rejection reasons include brand/trademark issues, quality concerns, and not meeting baseline connection criteria
Community docs (n8n) mention a security review before publishing, and Notion's docs say the listing's Authorization URL field only fills in after submission. Check whether either applies to you
gates.time_to_reach: Immediate for OAuth. 5-10 business days for a Marketplace listing review.

steps.title: Open the Notion Developer portal
steps.detail: Sign in to Notion with the account that belongs to your development workspace, then open the Developer portal. The old notion.so/my-integrations URL redirects to the same place.

steps.title: Create a new public connection
steps.detail: In the sidebar under Build, select Public connections, then Create new connection. Enter a connection name and choose your development workspace.
gotchas: Create a public connection, not an internal one or a personal access token. Those use static tokens and have no OAuth flow, so they won't work as a multi-user OAuth app.

steps.title: Choose the installation scope carefully
steps.detail: Pick 'Any workspace' if anyone outside your own workspaces will connect, or if you might want a Marketplace listing later. Pick 'Selected workspaces only' only for a fixed set of workspaces.
gotchas: Installation scope is set once and can't be changed. 'Selected workspaces only' connections can never be listed on the Marketplace.

steps.title: Select capabilities
steps.detail: Select only the capabilities your agent needs, such as read content, update content, or insert content. Users see these on the consent screen. They then use the page picker to choose which pages the connection can access.

steps.title: Add the redirect URI
steps.detail: In the redirect URI field, paste the callback URL shown in your Composio auth config, exactly as shown.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Use an exact match over HTTPS: no trailing slash, no fragments, no wildcards, no relative paths, no public IP addresses.
If you register more than one redirect URI, the token request must include redirect_uri.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret
steps.detail: Open the connection's Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID and client secret. Store them in a secret manager right away.
gotchas: Community notes say the secret may only be shown once.

steps.title: Add your credentials to a Composio auth config
steps.detail: In Composio, create a Notion auth config that uses your own developer credentials, and paste in the client ID and secret. Don't set any scopes, because Notion doesn't use OAuth scope strings.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio. This goes to api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize with owner=user, client_id, redirect_uri and response_type=code. Approve the consent screen, pick pages in the page picker, and confirm the code-for-token exchange at /v1/oauth/token succeeds.
gotchas: A wrong client ID doesn't return an OAuth error at the redirect. Notion only shows the problem on its consent page, so check the client ID if the install page looks wrong.

steps.title: Check how token refresh behaves
steps.detail: Check whether the token response includes a refresh_token, and test refreshing with grant_type=refresh_token at the same token endpoint. Notion's official docs describe refresh tokens, but an older community guide says tokens never expire and no refresh token is returned.

steps.title: Invite test users
steps.detail: Send your Composio connect link to test users in other workspaces (or in your selected workspaces). Each person must authorize separately and choose their own pages.

steps.title: Go live without a listing (optional: draft a Marketplace listing)
steps.detail: An Any-workspace connection already works for anyone through OAuth. If you want to be in Notion's directory, draft the listing text and assets using Notion's Connection Gallery Best Practices guide. Avoid trademark and brand problems, and make sure the connection meets Notion's baseline quality criteria.

steps.title: Submit the Marketplace listing
steps.detail: In the Marketplace dashboard, go to Listings > Connections, finish the listing draft, and submit it for review by the Notion team.

steps.title: Wait for Notion's listing review
steps.detail: Notion expects to reply by email within 5-10 business days. If it rejects the listing, the email explains why, and you can fix the issues and resubmit.

requirements.item: Connection name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope, capabilities
requirements.detail: All of these are required when you create the public connection.
No fragments, wildcards, relative paths, public IP addresses or trailing slash.
Required for a Marketplace listing, and it can't be changed after creation.
Community docs (n8n) say public distribution needs a company name and website in Organization Information. This wasn't confirmed on a Notion page.
Optional. Only needed if you want to appear in Notion's directory. Rejection reasons include brand/trademark issues, quality concerns, and not meeting baseline connection criteria.

scopes.effect: Shown on the consent screen. Lets the connection read pages the user shares in the page picker. Doesn't add any review.
Lets the connection edit pages the user shares. Shown on the consent screen.
Lets the connection create content in pages the user shares. Shown on the consent screen.

blockers.symptom: You need to list on the Marketplace or let any workspace install, but the connection was created as 'Selected workspaces only'.
blockers.cause: Installation scope is fixed when the connection is created.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with 'Any workspace' scope, then update the client ID and secret in Composio.

blockers.symptom: Redirect URI mismatch error during authorization or token exchange.
blockers.cause: The redirect URI doesn't exactly match what you registered (for example a trailing slash), or several URIs are registered and redirect_uri wasn't sent.
blockers.fix: Paste the Composio callback URL exactly as shown, and send redirect_uri in the token request.

blockers.symptom: The listing's Authorization URL field is empty.
blockers.cause: Notion's docs say this field only fills in after the public connection is submitted for review.
blockers.fix: Use the OAuth parameters (owner=user, client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code) through Composio for OAuth use, and submit for review if you need the listing URL.

blockers.cause: Brand/trademark issues, quality concerns, or not meeting baseline connection criteria.
blockers.fix: Fix the issues the email lists, check the Connection Gallery Best Practices guide, and resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Install page looks broken, but no OAuth error comes back.
blockers.cause: The client ID is wrong. Notion checks it on the consent page instead of returning an error at the redirect.
blockers.fix: Copy the client ID again from the Configuration tab into the Composio auth config.

composio.note: Composio's managed Notion app is the fastest way to start testing. Register your own public connection when you want your own client ID and secret, your own name on the consent screen, or a Marketplace listing. Notion has no OAuth scope strings, so leave scopes empty. Access comes from the connection's capabilities and the pages each user picks. Paste the callback URL from your Composio auth config into the connection's redirect URIs.

evidence.claim: Public connections are created in the Developer portal under Build > Public connections > Create new connection.
evidence.quote: In the Build section of the sidebar, select Public connections.

evidence.claim: Creating a connection requires a name, development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope and capabilities.
Installation scope is Any workspace (Marketplace-eligible) or Selected workspaces only (not eligible), and can't be changed after creation.
evidence.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can't be changed afterward.

evidence.claim: The OAuth client ID and secret are on the connection's Configuration tab; community notes say the secret may only be shown once.
The authorization URL takes owner=user, client_id, redirect_uri and response_type=code; state is optional.

open_questions: Do unlisted Any-workspace public connections have an install cap or stricter rate limits before Marketplace approval? Not found.
Does Notion require a security review before public distribution, as n8n's community docs claim, or only for Marketplace listings, as Notion's own docs suggest?
Refresh tokens: Notion's docs describe refresh_token, while Nango says tokens never expire. Check on a live app. The exact access-token lifetime wasn't confirmed.
The exact Marketplace review checklist (privacy policy, logo, demo, security questionnaire) wasn't confirmed; the Connection Gallery Best Practices page wasn't fetched.
